$comment: The behaviour id registry (#71, FR-007). The single source that scripts/floor-reporter.mjs,
mutations.json and the conformance matrix all read. Tests are keyed by ID, never by title,
so renaming a test does not silently drop coverage or break the mutation harness.

SEVENTEEN entries, sixteen of them APPLICABLE. The one that is not is generation determinism (SC-023), declared with applicable:false and the gate that discharges it named on the entry. It was deferred while the wrapper generator did not exist; #126 built the generator and its --check gate, and #75 WP04 settled it.

A behaviour with no applicable subject is either ABSENT from this file, or DECLARED with applicable:false and an inapplicableReason naming the gate that discharges it. It is never expressed as a skip and never deferred to a matrix cell — that was FR-010's earlier shape and it made the mission incoherent if the conformance matrix were dropped.

The second form is for a behaviour ADR-11 states as a CI-gate obligation rather than a runtime one: it has no test to mutate, but omitting it would leave the registry silently short of the ADR's list. #75 WP04 added the first, SC-023. Declaring one is not an escape hatch — config-contract asserts the applicable set equals ADR-11's list exactly, so nothing can be demoted to dodge a mutation, and it asserts the inapplicable set exactly too.
SUBJECTS (#73, FR-010). A behaviour id is no longer unique across the suite: sk-nav-pill
carries SC-006..SC-010 and SC-012, and the synthetic fixture carries them too. An id-only
coverage check therefore stayed GREEN with the ELEMENT's entire behaviour file deleted,
because the fixture still covered every id. That is this programme's certifying-absence
class, inside the reporter written to catch it.
Each subject names the FILE that must carry the id. scripts/floor-reporter.mjs checks
coverage per (id, subject file); scripts/suite-selftest.mjs's guard 7 compares mutations
against the same pairs, and a mutation's optional `subject` narrows which file's named
test it must red.
A subject's `name` is what tests/node/config-contract.test.ts matches against the ELEMENT
glob, so it names the element (sk-stub, sk-card, sk-nav-pill), not the test file's role. A
lens added a real element with no entry here and every gate went green — this registry was
the last hand-maintained list deciding whether an element is tested at all.
SC-002..SC-005 finally have a REAL subject (#74). They were written in #71 for this mission
and until now were carried only by the synthetic fixture — which is why the id-only coverage
check could not tell 'the fixture covers form association' from 'a shipped element does'.

#77 adds <sk-grid> as a subject of SC-013 and SC-014 — the two it genuinely owns. It is deliberately NOT added to SC-015: the registry guard is a claim about define(), not about any element that calls it, and listing every caller would make the id's subject list grow without adding an assertion.

#77 adds <sk-section-banner> as a subject of SC-013 and SC-014 on the same basis as <sk-grid>: it declares parts and adopts a generated sheet. It does not join SC-015, and does not claim an event or form id it does not have.

#78 adds <sk-feature-card> AND <sk-ribbon-card> as subjects of SC-013 and SC-014, on the same basis as #77's two: each declares parts and adopts a generated sheet. An earlier revision of this note named only feature-card while the data below added both.

#79 adds sk-button, sk-pill-tag and sk-check-bullet to SC-013 and SC-014. None claims an event or form id: button renders a real control and lets the platform supply the behaviour, and the other two are presentational.

#78 adds <sk-blog-card> to SC-013 and SC-014. Its SC-014 case is the only one in the repo that asserts TWO adopted sheets by identity and in order — the operator ruling has it compose sk-card's stylesheet rather than nest the element, so 'adopts the generated sheet' becomes 'adopts both, sk-card's first'.

#77 adds sk-site-footer to SC-013 and SC-014. Declaring the subject is what CREATES the obligation — nothing detects that a new element should have behaviour tests, and the suite's own floor proved it: with the tests written and passing but no subject declared, the run failed with '<sk-site-footer> exists but is not a subject of any behaviour ... it would ship with zero behaviour tests and every gate green'. That is the gate working.

#146 WP01 adds section-header to SC-013/SC-014 and adds status-indicator and entity-marker to SC-010/SC-013/SC-014. Slot projection and accessible naming remain direct assertions rather than mislabeled behavior ids.

#146 WP02 adds sk-action-row to SC-006/SC-007/SC-008/SC-010/SC-013/SC-014. SC-009 is intentionally absent because its activation request is non-cancelable and the component owns no preventable default action.
#146 WP03 adds react-action-row only to SC-006: its generated wrapper must deliver the action request once without changing the exact event or frozen detail identity.

#177 adds sk-card to SC-010. It was already an SC-013 subject and stays one; SC-010 is NEW to it because `status` is its first reflected STRING property — `variant` predates the id's adoption here and `inset` is boolean. Declaring the subject is what creates the obligation, per sk-site-footer's note above. sk-card is deliberately NOT added to SC-014: it adopts a generated sheet, but the claim there is asserted for it indirectly by sk-blog-card, whose two-sheet identity case imports sk-card's sheet by name, and adding a duplicate subject would grow the registry without adding an assertion. #177 also does not mint an id for fail-open: that behaviour is carried by SC-013, honestly rather than by relabelling, because a throw inside render() blanks the shadow root and the declared ::part() literally stops being targetable.

#147 WP03 records sk-metric and sk-evidence-chain as SC-013 subjects. Their approved WP01/WP02 fixture files already target every declared part; the shared registry is recorded here because config-contract derives every element and refuses an unregistered subject. No new behaviour id or SC-014 claim is added.

#178 adds sk-notice to NINE ids — SC-006..SC-010 and SC-011..SC-014 — which is the widest claim a single element has made here, and each one is owned rather than borrowed. SC-009 is the one worth stating: the element does NOT remove itself, so removal cannot be the default action a cancelable event prevents. What it prevents is the element's own FOCUS MOVE, which is the only post-dismissal effect the element owns; that is what keeps `cancelable` load-bearing instead of the inert flag sk-action-row correctly declined to claim. SC-011 is the FIRST shipped-element subject — until now only the synthetic fixture carried it — and sk-notice earns it with a marker slot that has real fallback content plus three named slots.
NO ID IS MINTED for the announcement contract, and that is the point of this note. ADR-11 has no id for 'a live region re-announces a changed message', and tests/node/config-contract.test.ts asserts the applicable set equals ADR-11's list exactly. The re-announcement and node-stability tests in sk-notice.test.ts therefore carry no [SC-NNN] marker. Fifth time this boundary has been reached (#140, #143, #77, #177); the answer is the same, and here it costs less than usual because the SC-010 arm that de-registers `message` reds the unmarked re-announcement test as well as the marked one — measured, not assumed.

#148 WP03 registers sk-bar-chart for SC-006/007/008/010/013/014 and react-bar-chart for SC-006/010. The element contributes seven mutation arms because SC-014 needs independent stylesheet-length and identity kills; the generated React wrapper contributes listener and property-reset arms.

#213 adds sk-check-bullet to SC-010 because state is its first reflected state axis and the fixture assigns pending before the late subclass is defined, then proves the property, reflected attribute, class, glyph, and accessible state text all survive upgrade. It remains passive and gains no event behaviour id.

#196 AND #204 CLOSE THAT BOUNDARY, and this note is where the count stops. The paragraph immediately above records the FIFTH mission to reach it (#140, #143, #77, #177, #178) and to answer it the same way: the coverage is real, it is simply held by an ordinary test rather than by the harness, because minting an id extends ADR-11 and #67 owns that. The operator ruled on 2026-09-07 that both pending cases be minted in ONE amendment — SC-016 for probe/rendered-control correspondence (#196) and SC-017 for a responsive threshold (#204) — each with a red-first mutation rather than a prose obligation. Neither of the two claims this docstring names as unowned is retro-fitted here: sk-notice's re-announcement contract and sk-card's vocabulary derivation are still unowned, still held by ordinary tests, and are NOT what these two ids cover. What changed is only that the route now exists.

SC-016 IS THE ONE ID IN THIS FILE THAT IS NOT INDEPENDENTLY BREAKABLE, and that is a property of the behaviour rather than of its tests. A correspondence claim is violated by any defect that breaks EITHER source, so with the assertion in place FOUR existing sk-form-input arms red it, measured before the entry was written rather than discovered afterwards: the merged-flag loop, the probe value sync, the pattern forwarding, and the type-before-value ordering. The last of those became SC-016's own arm; the pattern one was re-sited onto inputmode; the other two stay SC-003 and reach the correspondence test through the shared marker. The two ways to express that were `expectCollateral` on each of those arms, which would have removed guard 5's blast-radius bound from surgical arms to make room for one new id, and naming both ids on the shared test, which guard 4 and guard 5 both read. The second shipped: the correspondence test is marked `[SC-003][SC-016]`, the precedent being the `[SC-002][SC-003]` readonly test that has been in that file since #180.

#179 registers sk-time-series-chart for SC-006/007/008/009/010/013/014 and adds EIGHT arms. It claims NEITHER of the ids #196/#204 minted: SC-016 is delegate/rendered-control validity correspondence and this element has no form association, and SC-017 is a documented VIEWPORT threshold — this element documents none. Its marker-density limit is a data threshold, and the table scroller's region triad is MEASURED in updated() rather than gated on a breakpoint, precisely so there is no figure to drift from. Declining is the point: declaring a subject creates the obligation.
SC-009 IS CLAIMED, where sk-action-row correctly declined it. #179 requires a CANCELABLE event, and SC-009 is 'preventDefault demonstrably prevents where cancelable', so claiming it means naming a default action the ELEMENT owns. It owns exactly one: on activation it moves focus to the activated point's control. Selection is the application's and is never touched, so cancelling prevents the focus move and nothing else — the same shape sk-notice's entry records, and for the same reason its assertion is made against shadowRoot.activeElement rather than document.activeElement, which reports the host whether or not focus moved. The test activates with element.click(), not userEvent.click(): userEvent focuses the control first and the platform's own behaviour would satisfy the assertion for the wrong reason.
SC-013 CARRIES THE MISSION'S REQUIRED GAP ARM, and no id is minted for 'a null run breaks the line'. #179 asks for a mutation whose red is an interpolated gap; guard 7 keys every mutation on a declared (id, subject) pair and tests/node/config-contract.test.ts asserts the applicable set equals ADR-11's list exactly, so there is no id to mint here and mislabelling one is what this programme has refused repeatedly (#140, #143, #77, #177, #216). The honest binding is SC-013, because a gap here IS a declared ::part(): the arm filters the nulls out of the graphic's own seam, the line joins straight through, and the `gap` part stops existing. That is a mutation whose red is a part's ABSENCE — sk-card's #177 arm is the precedent — which is why the [SC-013] fixture mounts a series WITH an interior null run and a supplied gap threshold rather than only a dense one.
NO react-time-series-chart SUBJECT, stated rather than silent. The generated wrapper's first-render delivery of the nested structured series IS covered, by fixtures/react-consumer/src/sk-time-series-chart.test.tsx, which #148's own contract is modelled on. It is not declared as a subject because declaring it would add two more arms against the 129.1s of headroom this file's neighbour records (157 arms / 1276.4s at ee1d5be, 8.13s per arm) that this element's own eight arms already consume most of, and selftestCeilingSeconds is #225's, held by an operator ruling. Reversible by the next mission if the ceiling moves.

behaviours.summary: native form submit produces the expected FormData entry
setValidity blocks submission and the message reaches the a11y tree
form reset restores the initial value
a disabled control is excluded from submission
a property assigned before the definition loads is applied on upgrade
content reaches the intended slot; fallback appears when empty
Escape closes, focus returns to the invoker, aria-expanded tracks state
every declared ::part() is present and targetable from outside
behaviours.note: Subject-owned. Shipped elements declare styling hooks with @csspart and render matching part= surfaces; expected-parts.json rejects manifest drift, while every registered subject fixture proves its declared parts are present and externally targetable. The synthetic fixture remains as harness self-coverage.

behaviours.summary: adopts a constructed stylesheet by identity and injects no <style> element
a second define warns, keeps the original constructor, and is silent for the same constructor
an element that derives a validity flag from an object other than the rendered control agrees with that control for the same intended state
behaviours.note: ADR-11 item 10 (#196, operator ruling 2026-09-07). Element-owned, not fixture-owned: the synthetic fixture has no UA delegate to desynchronize, and a fixture-owned id would carry the same defect behaviours.json's own docstring records for SC-002..SC-005 — a green that cannot tell 'the fixture covers it' from 'a shipped element does'. sk-form-input is the only element in this repository with a delegate today; sk-form-textarea deliberately has none (ADR-14, 'Corrected premise'), so it is NOT a subject and declaring it one would assert nothing.

behaviours.summary: a documented viewport threshold is declared at the documented figure and the behaviour it gates actually changes at it
behaviours.note: ADR-11 item 11 (#204, operator ruling 2026-09-07). THE HEIGHT THRESHOLD IS DECLARATION-ONLY, recorded here rather than left to be reconstructed from ADR prose: the lane runs at 414x, so `(max-width: 720px)` is reachable live and `(max-height: 480px)` is not. The width arm reds both the sheet-reading and the live assertion; the height arm reds the sheet-reading one alone, which is the whole red available for it in this lane. Item 11's live clause is scoped to thresholds the lane can reach, and a future lane that can shrink the viewport should add the live half rather than assume it exists. The id #182 could not use: guard 7 keys on a declared (id, subject) pair and tests/node/config-contract.test.ts pins the applicable set to ADR-11's list, so sk-page-header's two reflow blocks shipped with real tests and no re-derived red. Element-owned because the threshold lives in the element's own generated stylesheet, which is what the arms mutate.

behaviours.summary: regenerating wrappers from an unchanged manifest is a no-op, and drift fails CI
behaviours.inapplicableReason: ADR-11 item 9 assigns this to the NODE lane and states it as two clauses: regeneration is a no-op, AND drift fails CI. Both are enforced by scripts/build-react-wrappers.mjs --check, which generates twice and compares byte-for-byte before comparing against the committed tree, as an ENFORCED lint-code step with two REQUIRED_LINT entries. It is not a mutation-harness behaviour: suite-selftest.mjs runs the browser project only, and extending it to the node lane would add ~1.8s to each of 44 runs (~240s against a 180s ceiling) to re-prove what a --check gate already proves. Declared here rather than omitted so the registry mirrors ADR-11's list entry for entry and the discharge is recorded where a reader looks. A COUNT OF ANOTHER FILE'S LIST IS DELIBERATELY NOT WRITTEN HERE: this sentence said 'ADR-11's fifteen' and went stale the moment #196/#204 made it seventeen. The docstring at the top of THIS file does still carry a count, and that is a different thing — it counts the entries immediately below it, which a reader can check in the same file and tests/node/config-contract.test.ts asserts the applicable half of. A count of a list that lives somewhere else is the one nothing re-derives.
